title: The use of beta-agonists and the risk of death and near death from asthma
authors: Spitzer WO, Suissa S, Ernst P, Horwitz RI, Habbick B, Cockcroft D, et al.
followUp: 47,842 person-years in the source cohort, 1980 to 1987
population: 129 cases of fatal (44) or near-fatal (85) asthma and 655 matched controls drawn from 12,301 Saskatchewan residents aged 5 to 54 years with at least 10 asthma drug prescriptions, 1978 to 1987
funder: Supported by a grant from Boehringer-Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Canada, Ltd.; the paper states that the study was funded entirely by Boehringer-Ingelheim, which has a commercial interest in one of the products assessed, and that a Scientific Advisory Board reviewed the protocol and the main results. Two authors held Fonds de la Recherche en Santé du Québec scholarships and two held Canadian national health research awards.
result: Use of beta-agonists by metered-dose inhaler was associated with death from asthma (odds ratio 2.6 per canister per month, 95% CI 1.7 to 3.9) and with death or near death combined (1.9, 1.6 to 2.4). Per canister per month, the odds ratio for death was 5.4 for fenoterol (200 µg per puff) and 2.4 for albuterol (100 µg per puff); per 100 µg, 2.3 against 2.4. The crude albuterol odds ratio of 0.9 rose to 2.8 after adjustment for fenoterol use. Among those not hospitalised in the previous 2 years, the odds ratio for death remained 2.4 (1.3 to 4.7) for albuterol. Crude asthma death rates, which the authors call unusable for comparison: 9.2 per 10,000 person-years overall, 8.6 with albuterol, 34.6 with fenoterol and 1.8 with neither. At most 7 of the 44 deaths might have been sudden and possibly cardiac; the authors could not separate drug effects from markers of more severe asthma.
